subject: zoology_2
question_text: Name different types of papillae present on the tongue of man.

verification.note: Sourced from 'My Baby Bullet-Q — Senior Inter Zoology' (Star-Q Pass Track Series, Sri Publishers, 2022), book p.46, VSAQ 52. The printed exam years are the book's claim, reproduced here as appearances. Zoology-II holds only ONE source book in the corpus, so the two-book union check is structurally impossible for this card; 'not checked' does NOT mean 'checked and clean'. The mark split is our reading of the question and is a claim until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it.

insider_note: Half the marks are for the locations. Naming the three types alone is a half answer.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: The three types
steps.why: The papillae are the small projections that carry the taste buds, so naming them is naming the taste surface of the tongue.
common_mistakes: Naming taste buds instead of papillae. Taste buds sit on the papillae.
Giving only two types. Three are expected.
steps.memory_tip: Fungiform, filiform, circumvallate — mushroom, thread, walled.
steps.margin_note: Name all three first, then place them.
lines: Papillae are small projections on the upper
surface of the tongue. There are 3 types:

steps.label: Their locations
steps.why: Each type keeps to its own zone of the tongue, so the location is what tells them apart.
common_mistakes: Placing circumvallate papillae at the tip. They lie at the base.
Giving no locations at all. Half the marks are here.
steps.memory_tip: Tip and margin, whole surface, base — in that order.
steps.margin_note: One line each. Keep the same order as above.
